next.name: Threat Group-3390
next.headline: Threat Group-3390: a China-linked group known by many names, with tools and a Mimi chat app report
next.in_short: Threat Group-3390 goes by many names, including Emissary Panda and APT27. Cards tie it to a Mimi chat app compromise and to past use of Scanbox, though attribution there is low-confidence.

sentences.t: Threat Group-3390 is also known as Earth Smilodon, TG-3390, Emissary Panda, BRONZE UNION, APT27, Iron Tiger, LuckyMouse and Linen Typhoon.
Recorded Future's Insikt Group lists LuckyMouse (TG-3390, Emissary Panda, Bronze Union) among actors that have used the Scanbox framework in the past.
The catalogue lists many tools for the group, including PlugX, Cobalt Strike, Mimikatz, Impacket, China Chopper, HyperBro, gh0st RAT, ZxShell, SysUpdate and RCSession.
Scanbox is a reconnaissance framework that lets attackers track website visitors. Insikt Group says it has features for keylogging and for delivering additional malware.
The report on the Iron Tiger compromise of the chat application Mimi lists HyperBro samples for Windows and Rshell samples for Linux and Mac OS.

A threat report is titled 'Iron Tiger Compromises Chat Application Mimi, Targets Windows, Mac, and Linux Users'. It is mostly a list of indicators, such as file hashes and command-and-control addresses.
In March 2019, Insikt Group found two Scanbox campaigns. One was a compromised Pakistani government passport tracking page. The other was a spoofed Central Tibetan Administration website.

Insikt Group says the attackers likely meant to profile visitors' devices for follow-on intrusions. It assesses with low confidence that Chinese state-sponsored actors were behind them. The cards do not tie these two campaigns to TG-3390 itself.
